findings.heading: Demographic pyramids and Likert-scales
findings.proposition: The five-point Likert example scale contains "Disagree" as its fourth option; the Turkish list gives "Katılıyorum" (Agree) twice and never gives "Katılmıyorum" (Disagree).
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader sees a five-point scale with a duplicated "Agree" and no "Disagree", so the worked example of a Likert scale is internally inconsistent and cannot be used as a model for coding response categories.

findings.heading: **apyramid** package / Linelist data
findings.proposition: The grey background bars show the range of the un-faceted data for that age group; the Turkish text instead says the grey bars show the range of un-faceted data "such as age group" ("yaş grubu gibi yönlü olmayan verilerin aralığını"), making age group an example of un-faceted data rather than the grouping the range is computed within.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader misreads what the grey background bars represent and cannot tell that each grey bar is the total for that age group across all facets.

findings.heading: **apyramid** package / Missing values
findings.proposition: Rows with NA in split_by or age_group do not trigger the FACETING described in the previous section; the Turkish text says instead that such rows "do not affect the formation of the graph" ("grafiğin oluşmasını etkilemez").
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader loses the link to the faceting rule just above (NA is not counted as a third split_by value) and is told a broader, false claim that missing rows have no effect on the plot at all, which is contradicted two sentences later by na.rm = FALSE.

findings.heading: **apyramid** package / Missing values
findings.proposition: With na.rm = FALSE the missing rows appear in TWO distinct places: in an adjacent bar plot, and as a separate age group at the top of the pyramid; the Turkish text collapses this into one place, "at the top, in a separate adjacent bar chart".
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader does not expect a new age-category row at the top of the pyramid and may read that extra category as a data error rather than as the missing-age group.

findings.heading: `ggplot()`
findings.proposition: After the axis flip the two bar plots stand vertically with their bases meeting in the middle of the plot; the Turkish sentence omits that the bases meet in the plot middle.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader is not told why one series is negated, so the geometric reason the two histograms join at zero to form the pyramid is missing from the method overview.
